data.long_meaning: Devaki is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘deva’, meaning ‘god’. The name signifies a goddess or a divine being. In Hindu mythology, Devaki is the name of the mother of Lord Krishna. The name Devaki carries the meaning “Goddess, Divine” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devaki usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess, divine and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carrier of the divine, blessed with divine grace

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devaki total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Devaki is a revered name in Hindu culture and is associated with the divine. The name is sometimes used as a feminine form of the divine name Deva. It is also commonly used as a matronymic name, with women named Devaki being referred to as “Devaki maa” or "mother Devaki". In some communities, the name Devaki is given to girls born on a Saturday, further cementing its connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: Devaki, as the name of Lord Krishna’s mother, holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. As a goddess and the mother of the god Vishnu himself, Devaki embodies the divine feminine and represents the nurturing, protective, and unconditional love of a mother. Her story, where her womb is chosen to give birth to Lord Krishna despite her own suffering, is a powerful reminder of the selflessness and sacredness of motherhood. The name Devaki is thus a reminder of the divine presence in all aspects of life, particularly in the bond between mother and child.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Devaki is a Sanskrit name meaning 'Goddess of the Milk Ocean'. It symbolizes the divine power of the sacred womb, nurturing the divine child within, even in the midst of great adversity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Devaki was the daughter of King Vidura and sister of Bhishma Pitamaha in Mahabharata. The name Devaki carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that describes the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and Kaurava princes, and is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. Devaki is mentioned as the sister of Bhishma and the mother of Krishna.

historical_references.reference: Devaki was also the name of a queen consort of the ancient Indian king Chandragupta Maurya, who ruled around 321-297 BC.
historical_references.context: Chandragupta Maurya was a prominent ruler of the Maurya Empire in ancient India. Devaki is mentioned as one of his consorts in historical texts.

modern_usage.modern_context: Devaki is a significant character in Hindu mythology as the mother of the god Krishna, who was prophesied to destroy the demon king Kamsa. Her story is popularly retold in various formats, including books, movies, and television series. In contemporary literature, Devaki's story is often explored in depth, offering insights into motherhood, sacrifice, and the complexities of destiny. In Indian cinema, there have been several adaptations of the Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita, which feature Devaki as a prominent character. On television, there have been various serials and mythological shows that have retold her story, often with a modern twist. Overall, Devaki continues to be a source of inspiration and intrigue, particularly for those interested in Hindu mythology and spirituality.
